results.title: LU decomposition without pivoting
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $A$ an $n \times n$ matrix over $K$ whose leading principal minors are all nonzero: for every $k \le n$, the determinant of the upper-left $k \times k$ block of $A$ is nonzero. Then $A = LU$ for some $n \times n$ matrices $L$ and $U$ over $K$ such that $L$ is lower triangular with every diagonal entry equal to $1$ and $U$ is upper triangular.

results.title: Uniqueness of the LU decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $A$ an invertible $n \times n$ matrix over $K$. Suppose $A = L_1 U_1 = L_2 U_2$, where $L_1$ and $L_2$ are lower triangular $n \times n$ matrices over $K$ with every diagonal entry equal to $1$, and $U_1$ and $U_2$ are upper triangular $n \times n$ matrices over $K$. Then $L_1 = L_2$ and $U_1 = U_2$.

results.title: Prime-counting criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers and let $\pi(n)$ be the number of primes at most $n$. If $n! \cdot (k+n-1)^{\pi(n)} < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.

results.title: Half-exponent criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers. If $n! \cdot (k+n-1)^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1} < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.

results.title: Quadratic starts give a large prime in a consecutive block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 38$ and $k > n^2$ be natural numbers. Then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.

results.title: Square-root and primorial criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers, write $N = k + n - 1$, and let $P(n)$ denote the product of all primes at most $n$. If $n! \cdot N^{\lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor + 1} \cdot P(n) < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.

results.title: Erdős layer criterion for a large prime in a consecutive block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $1 \le n < k$ be natural numbers, write $N = k + n - 1$ and $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$, and for a natural number $m$ let $P(m)$ denote the product of all primes at most $m$. If $n! \cdot P(n) \cdot \prod_{i=2}^{L} P(\lfloor N^{1/i} \rfloor) < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.

results.title: Erdős layer criterion with a one-third first layer for a large prime in a consecutive block
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n < k$ be natural numbers, write $N = k + n - 1$ and $L = \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$, assume $N \ge 6$, and for a natural number $m$ let $P(m)$ denote the product of all primes at most $m$. If $n! \cdot P(\lfloor N/3 \rfloor) \cdot \prod_{i=2}^{L} P(\lfloor N^{1/i} \rfloor) < k^n$, then some prime $p > n$ divides one of the integers $k, k+1, \dots, k+n-1$.

results.title: Large starts give a large prime in a consecutive block
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Simply normal numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $b$ and a real number $x$, write $a_k$ for the $k$-th base-$b$ digit of $x$ after the radix point, counting from $k = 0$. Then $x$ is simply normal in base $b$ if for every natural number $d < b$ the proportion $\#\{k < n : a_k = d\} / n$ tends to $1/b$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Normal numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $b$ and a real number $x$, write $a_i$ for the $i$-th base-$b$ digit of $x$ after the radix point, counting from $i = 0$. results.title: Next label/state code of a situation

results.title: Push-count table of a situation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix an encoding record $E$ of a finite multi-stack machine. For a situation $i$ and a stack number $k$, $\mathrm{pl}(i, k)$ is the number of symbols that the effect of situation $i$ has pushed onto the stack that the inverse stack numbering of $E$ assigns to $k$ and that are still on top of that stack at the end of the step.

results.title: Consumption table of a situation
results.caption: Definition

For a situation $i$ and a stack number $k$, $\mathrm{cn}(i, k)$ is the number of original symbols that the effect of situation $i$ consumes from the stack that the inverse stack numbering of $E$ assigns to $k$; a symbol pushed and then popped within the same step is not counted.

results.title: Pushed-symbol table of a situation
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Idle-extended step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite TM2 machine $M$ and a configuration $c$, the idle-extended step of $M$ at $c$ is the configuration that one step of $M$ produces from $c$ when the label of $c$ is not the halted label, and is $c$ itself when it is (a halted configuration stays put).

results.title: Idle-extended run
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite TM2 machine $M$ and a configuration $c$, the idle-extended run of $M$ from $c$ is the sequence of configurations whose term at time $0$ is $c$ and whose term at time $t + 1$ is the idle-extended step of $M$ applied to its term at time $t$.

results.summary: For an assignment $a$, given as a list of booleans, and a variable index $v \in \mathbb{N}$, the variable $v$ is true under $a$ when $v$ is less than the length of $a$ and the entry of $a$ at position $v$ is true. In particular, variables with index at least the length of $a$ are not true.

results.title: L0 (a satisfied dense clause has a satisfied listed literal)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\ell$ be a list of pairs $(p, b)$ of a variable index $p \in \mathbb{N}$ and a sign $b$ (true or false), and let $a$ be a list of booleans. If $a$ satisfies the dense clause over $V$ variables built from $\ell$, then some pair $(p, b) \in \ell$ has $p$ less than the length of $a$ and $a_p = b$.

results.title: Stack cap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $T$ and $d$ (an input bound, a run length and a per-step growth), the stack cap is $H = m + (T + 1) d + 1$.

results.title: Faithful literal list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A list $\ell$ of literals $(p, b)$, each a variable index $p \in \mathbb{N}$ with a sign $b$, is faithful for $V \in \mathbb{N}$ when every literal $(p, b)$ of $\ell$ has $p < V$ and the first literal of $\ell$ with index $p$ is $(p, b)$.

results.title: Faithful dense clause family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is a faithful family over $V$ variables when every clause of $\varphi$ is the dense clause over $V$ variables built from some list of literals that is faithful for $V$.

results.title: Faithful dense clause family with positive literals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A CNF formula $\varphi$ is a faithful family with positive literals over $V$ variables when every clause of $\varphi$ is the dense clause over $V$ variables built from some list $\ell$ of literals that is faithful for $V$ and contains a positive literal $(p, \mathrm{true})$ for some $p$.

results.title: Exact clause semantics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\ell$ be a list of pairs $(p, b)$ of a variable index $p$ and a sign $b$ that is faithful for $V$, and let $a$ be a list of Booleans. Then $a$ satisfies the dense clause over $V$ variables built from $\ell$ if and only if some $(p, b) \in \ell$ has $p < |a|$ and $a_p = b$.

results.title: The all-true assignment satisfies a faithful clause with a positive literal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\ell$ be a list of literals that is faithful for $V$ and contains a positive literal $(p, \mathrm{true})$. Then the all-true assignment of length $V$ satisfies the dense clause over $V$ variables built from $\ell$.

results.title: A form yielding the empty word contains no terminal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a context-free grammar over terminals $T$ and let $\alpha$ be a sentential form of $G$. If $\alpha$ yields the empty word in $G$, then no terminal symbol $a \in T$ occurs in $\alpha$.

results.title: Productions without terminals of an encoded grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar with the same start nonterminal whose productions are the productions of $g$, in their order, whose right-hand sides contain no terminal.

results.title: Computed nullable nonterminals of an encoded grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the list of generating nonterminals of the encoded grammar that has the start nonterminal of $g$ and, as productions, the productions of $g$ whose right-hand sides contain no terminal.

results.title: Yields of the empty word need only terminal-free productions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and $\alpha$ a sentential form of the grammar $g$ denotes. If $\alpha$ yields the empty word in that grammar, then $\alpha$ also yields the empty word in the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar consisting of the productions of $g$ that contain no terminal.

results.title: Terminal-free productions yield only the empty word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and consider the grammar of its productions without terminals. If a sentential form $\alpha$ that contains no terminal yields a word $w$ in that grammar, then $w$ is the empty word.

results.title: Yields in the terminal-free subgrammar are yields of the grammar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar, $\alpha$ a sentential form and $w$ a word. If $\alpha$ yields $w$ in the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar consisting of the productions of $g$ that contain no terminal, then $\alpha$ yields $w$ in the grammar $g$ denotes.

results.title: The nullable nonterminals are computed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$ and every natural number $A$, $A$ belongs to the computed list of nullable nonterminals of $g$ (the generating nonterminals of the productions of $g$ without terminals) if and only if $A$ is nullable in the grammar denoted by $g$, that is, $A$ derives the empty word.

results.title: Deleting nonterminals from an encoded right-hand side
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $N$ be a list of natural numbers and $u$ an encoded right-hand side, that is, a word whose letters are nonterminals $i \in \mathbb{N}$ or terminals. The result is the list of all words obtained from $u$ by deleting some of the occurrences of nonterminals that belong to $N$ (possibly none, possibly all) and keeping every other letter in order; each choice of deleted occurrences contributes one entry of the list.

For every encoded word $u$ and every sentential form $\alpha$ of the grammar denoted by $g$, $\alpha$ is obtained from the decoding of $u$ by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals of the grammar denoted by $g$ if and only if $\alpha$ is the decoding of a word obtained from $u$ by deleting some occurrences of nonterminals in the computed list of nullable…

results.title: Removing empty productions from an encoded grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar with the same start nonterminal whose productions are, for each production $A \to u$ of $g$, the productions $A \to v$ for every nonempty word $v$ obtained from $u$ by deleting some occurrences of nonterminals in the computed list of nullable nonterminals of $g$.

results.title: Productions of the computable removal of empty productions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, a production is a production of the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions if and only if it is a production of the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating empty productions.

results.title: Computable removal of empty productions agrees with the classical one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the grammar denoted by the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions is equal to the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating empty productions: from each production, all productions obtained by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals from its output, except those with empty output.

results.title: Removing empty productions drops only the empty word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the language of the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions consists of the nonempty words of the language of $g$.

results.title: Nonterminals of an encoded grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the list obtained by duplicate removal from the list made of the start nonterminal of $g$ followed, for each production of $g$ in order, by its left-hand side and then the nonterminals of its right-hand side in order. It lists without repetitions the nonterminals that $g$ mentions.

results.title: Target of a unit right-hand side
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded right-hand side $u$, a list whose entries are nonterminals $i \in \mathbb{N}$ or terminals, the optional value is $B$ when $u$ consists of the single nonterminal $B$, and there is no value otherwise.

results.title: One round of unit reachability
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, a natural number $A$ and a list $S$ of natural numbers, the list consisting of $A$ followed, for each production of $g$ in order whose left-hand side lies in $S$ and whose right-hand side is a single nonterminal $B$, by that nonterminal $B$.

results.title: Nonterminals reachable by unit productions in an encoded grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$ and a natural number $A$, let $n$ be the number of distinct nonterminals mentioned in $g$ (the start, the left-hand sides, and the nonterminals on right-hand sides). The list is obtained from the empty list by applying one round of unit reachability from $A$ exactly $n + 1$ times.

results.title: Unit reachability is computed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and let $A$ and $B$ be natural numbers. Then $B$ belongs to the computed list of nonterminals reachable from $A$ by unit productions of $g$ if and only if there are $k \ge 0$ and nonterminals $A = C_0, C_1, \dots, C_k = B$ such that $C_{i-1} \to C_i$ is a production of the grammar denoted by $g$ for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le k$.

results.title: Unit elimination for encoded grammars
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar with the start nonterminal of $g$ whose productions are listed as follows: for each nonterminal $A$ in the list of nonterminals of $g$, and for each production $B \to u$ of $g$ in order such that $B$ is in the computed list of nonterminals reachable from $A$ by unit productions and $u$ is not a single nonterminal, the production $A \to u$.

results.title: Productions of the encoded unit elimination
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar over terminals $T$ and let $r$ be a production with terminals in $T$ and nonterminals in $\mathbb{N}$. Then $r$ is a production of the grammar denoted by the encoded unit elimination of $g$ if and only if $r$ is a production of the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating unit productions.

results.title: The encoded unit elimination denotes the unit-eliminated grammar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the grammar denoted by the encoded unit elimination of $g$ is equal to the grammar obtained from the grammar denoted by $g$ by eliminating unit productions.

results.title: Reduction of an encoded grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$, the encoded grammar obtained by first removing the empty productions of $g$ (encoded $\varepsilon$-elimination) and then removing the unit productions of the result (encoded unit elimination).

results.title: The reduced grammar generates the language minus the empty word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, the language of the reduction of $g$ (empty productions removed, then unit productions removed) consists of the nonempty words of the language of $g$.

results.title: The reduced grammar has no empty and no unit productions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every encoded context-free grammar $g$, every production of the grammar denoted by the reduction of $g$ (empty productions removed, then unit productions removed) has a nonempty output, and that output is not a single nonterminal.

results.title: Reduction is primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a type of terminals with a primitive recursive encoding. The map sending an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ to its reduction, the encoded grammar obtained from $g$ by removing empty productions and then unit productions, is primitive recursive, where encoded grammars are encoded as pairs of a start nonterminal and a list of productions.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $h : S \times B \to S$ be a compression function and $iv \in S$ an initial value. The chaining value of a list of blocks given last block first is defined recursively: the empty list has chaining value $iv$, and a list with first entry $x$ followed by a list $xs$ has chaining value $h(c, x)$, where $c$ is the chaining value of $xs$.

results.title: Merkle–Damgård chaining value
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $h : S \times B \to S$ be a compression function and $iv \in S$ an initial value. The chaining value of a list of blocks $M = (x_1, \dots, x_L)$ is $z_L$, where $z_0 = iv$ and $z_i = h(z_{i-1}, x_i)$ for $1 \le i \le L$.

results.title: Merkle–Damgård hash with length strengthening
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $h : S \times B \to S$ be a compression function, $iv \in S$ an initial value and $\ell : \mathbb{N} \to B$ a length encoding. The hash of a list of blocks $M = (x_1, \dots, x_L)$ is $h(z_L, \ell(L))$, where $z_0 = iv$ and $z_i = h(z_{i-1}, x_i)$ for $1 \le i \le L$.

results.title: Collision of a compression function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $h : S \times B \to S$ be a compression function. A pair $(p_1, p_2)$ of compression inputs in $S \times B$ is a collision of $h$ when $p_1 \ne p_2$ and $h(p_1) = h(p_2)$.

results.title: Core allocation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A payoff vector $x \colon N \to \mathbb{R}$ is a core allocation of a cooperative game $v$ on a finite set $N$ of players if it is efficient, $\sum_{i \in N} x_i = v(N)$, and coalitionally rational, $v(S) \le \sum_{i \in S} x_i$ for every coalition $S \subseteq N$.

results.title: Balanced cooperative game
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A cooperative game $v$ on a finite set $N$ of players is balanced if for every family of real weights $(\lambda_S)_{S \subseteq N}$ with $\lambda_S \ge 0$ for every coalition $S \subseteq N$ and $\sum_{S \subseteq N,\, i \in S} \lambda_S = 1$ for every player $i \in N$, one has $\sum_{S \subseteq N} \lambda_S \, v(S) \le v(N)$.

results.title: Bondareva–Shapley theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $v$ be a cooperative game with transferable utility on a finite set $N$ of players. Then $v$ has a core allocation $x \colon N \to \mathbb{R}$, that is, the core of $v$ is nonempty, if and only if $v$ is balanced.
